source_title: ‘SCTV’ Netflix Documentary Shares Unseen Footage of Catherine O’Hara Months Before Her Death - People.com
source_excerpt:
The documentary is the final on-screen appearance for the actress
Catherine O’Hara appears in Netflix’s new documentary SCTV: The Greatest Show You’ve Never Heard Of
The documentary is the final on-screen appearance by the comedic actress, who got her start in Second City Toronto and went on to a decades-long storied career
The actress died at the age of 71 on Friday, Jan. 30
Catherine O’Hara is treated with reverence in her final on-screen appearance.
The late Beetlejuice actress participated in the new Netflix documentary SCTV: The Greatest Show You’ve Never Heard Of , produced by Jimmy Kimmel . O’Hara appeared with fellow SCTV alumni Eugene Levy , Martin Short , Andrea Martin and Dave Thomas, reminiscing together about the time they shared on the Canadian comedy-turned-network-cult classic.
O’Hara got her start at The Second City Toronto and, through her hilarious performances, worked her way up to the company’s leading female comic as SCTV came together. In 1981, she left SCTV when she was hired in the retooled cast of Saturday Night Live , only to return when SCTV moved from local Canadian broadcasting to a spot in the NBC lineup.
In the documentary, O’Hara shared her memories of the show’s 1984 finale. She said, “I grew up really with these people, coming out of high school and then getting to work with these amazing, beautiful, talented, fun, funny people for my formative years.”
“That kind of comedy is just perfect when you’re in your 20s because you’re cocky at that age,” she continued. “And it’s Second City. You have a place to express it in a funny way, and you’ve been told you’re funny enough to be here.”
The documentary closes with a dedication to the cast members that SCTV has lost in the years since it aired. Showing photos of each, it read, “John Candy died in 1994. He was 43. Harold Ramis died in 2014. He was 69. Joe Flaherty died in 2024. He was 82.”
The camera follows O’Hara as she bids farewell to her castmates and closes with scenes of her from SCTV . The screen then reads, “Catherine O’Hara died in 2026. She was 71.”
Levy worked with O’Hara several times throughout their five decades of friendship, including as Johnny and Moira Rose on the hit sitcom Schitt’s Creek , which also starred their on-screen kids Dan Levy (David Rose) and Annie Murphy (Alexis Rose).
Eugene, 79, remembered his decades-long friendship with O’Hara in a statement shared with PEOPLE after news of her death became public.
“Words seem inadequate to express the loss I feel today,” the actor said. “I had the honor of knowing and working with the great Catherine O’Hara for over fifty years.”
“From our beginnings on the Second City stage, to SCTV, to the movies we did with Chris Guest, to our six glorious years on Schitt’s Creek , I cherished our working relationship, but most of all our friendship,” Eugene continued. “And I will miss her. My heart goes out to Bo, Matthew, Luke, and the entire O’Hara family.”
